prompt.adult: Proverbs 25:11 compares a word fitly spoken to something in settings of silver. What is it like?
prompt.child: A Proverb says the right words at the right time are beautiful. What does it compare them to?
prompt.teen: Proverbs 25:11: “A word fitly spoken is like” what “In settings of silver”?
prompt.older: According to Proverbs 25:11, what is a word fitly spoken like?

verses.text: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold In settings of silver.

explanation.adult: Read the middle of 25:11, just before “In settings of silver.”
explanation.child: Look at the words right after “is like” in verse 11.
explanation.teen: 25:11 has two lines; the picture begins at the end of the first. Read it.

teaching.extended_explanation: 25:11 belongs to the collection that 25:1 calls “proverbs of Solomon.” Its picture comes in the first line, and the setting in the second.
teaching.takeaway: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.

prompt.adult: Proverbs 31:1 introduces words that a king’s mother taught him. What was the king’s name?
prompt.child: Proverbs 31 begins with advice a mother gave her son, who was a king. What was his name?
prompt.older: According to Proverbs 31:1, whose mother taught him this utterance?

verses.text: The words of King Lemuel, the utterance which his mother taught him:

explanation.child: Look at the very start of Proverbs 31:1.
explanation.teen: 31:1 names the king and then says who taught him. Read the name.
explanation.older: It follows “The words of King” in 31:1.

teaching.extended_explanation: 31:1 says the utterance came from the king’s mother. 31:2 opens her words with three questions to her son.
teaching.takeaway: These are “The words of King Lemuel.”

prompt.adult: Proverbs 25:1 says some proverbs of Solomon were copied by the men of a later king. Which king?
prompt.child: Some of Solomon’s wise sayings were copied down later by a king’s men. Which king?
prompt.teen: Proverbs 25:1: “These also are proverbs of Solomon which the men of” whom “copied”?
prompt.older: According to Proverbs 25:1, whose men copied these proverbs of Solomon?

verses.text: These also are proverbs of Solomon which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied:
As the heavens for height and the earth for depth, So the heart of kings is unsearchable.

explanation.adult: Read the middle of 25:1, after “the men of.”
explanation.child: Look in the middle of verse 1.
explanation.teen: 25:1 names Solomon first and then the later king. Read the second name.

teaching.extended_explanation: 25:1 opens a new collection of Solomon’s proverbs. 25:3 says the heart of kings is unsearchable, as the heavens for height and the earth for depth.
teaching.takeaway: The men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied them.

prompt.adult: Proverbs 25:25 compares good news from a far country to something. What?
prompt.child: A Proverb says hearing good news from far away feels like something. Like what?
prompt.teen: Proverbs 25:25: what is “good news from a far country” like?
prompt.older: According to Proverbs 25:25, to what is good news from a far country compared?

choices.text: shade to a worker in the heat
cold water to a weary soul

verses.text: As cold water to a weary soul, So is good news from a far country.
A righteous man who falters before the wicked Is like a murky spring and a polluted well.

explanation.child: Look at the start of verse 25.
explanation.teen: 25:25 gives the picture first and the good news second. Read the first line.

teaching.extended_explanation: 25:26 follows with a darker picture: a righteous man who falters before the wicked is like a murky spring and a polluted well.
teaching.takeaway: Good news from a far country is “As cold water to a weary soul.”

prompt.adult: Agur asks God for two things before he dies. In 30:8, what does he ask God to give him?
prompt.child: Agur asks God for two things. In one of them, what does he ask God to give him?
prompt.older: According to Proverbs 30:8, what does Agur ask God to give him?

verses.text: Two things I request of You (Deprive me not before I die):
Remove falsehood and lies far from me; Give me neither poverty nor riches— Feed me with the food allotted to me;

explanation.adult: Read the middle of 30:8, after “Give me.”
explanation.child: Look in the middle of verse 8.
explanation.teen: 30:8 holds both requests; the second begins with “Give me.” Read on from there.

teaching.extended_explanation: 30:7 says he asks before he dies. 30:8 begins by asking that falsehood and lies be removed far from him.
teaching.takeaway: He asked, “Give me neither poverty nor riches.”

prompt.adult: Proverbs 4:23 calls for guarding the heart with all diligence. In 25:28, a man with no rule over his own spirit is like what?
prompt.child: Proverbs 25 describes a person who cannot control himself. What is he like?
prompt.teen: Proverbs 25:28: whoever “has no rule over his own spirit” is like what?
prompt.older: Alongside the guarded heart of 4:23, to what does 25:28 compare the man without self-rule?

choices.text: a ship tossed without a rudder
a city broken down, without walls
a field where the hedge is torn down

verses.text: Keep your heart with all diligence, For out of it spring the issues of life.
Whoever has no rule over his own spirit Is like a city broken down, without walls.

explanation.child: Look at the end of verse 28.
explanation.teen: 4:23 is the setting; 25:28 names the man first and his picture second. Read the second line.

teaching.extended_explanation: 4:23 says the issues of life spring out of the heart. 25:28 opens by naming the one who has no rule over his own spirit.
teaching.takeaway: He “Is like a city broken down, without walls.”

prompt.adult: Proverbs 4:7 calls wisdom the principal thing. In 2:4, the son is told to search for her as for what?
prompt.child: Proverbs 2 says to look hard for wisdom, the way people search for something valuable. What?
prompt.teen: Proverbs 2:4: “And search for her as for” what?
prompt.older: Proverbs 4:7 urges, “Therefore get wisdom.” According to 2:4, what is wisdom to be searched for like?

verses.text: If you seek her as silver, And search for her as for hidden treasures;
Wisdom is the principal thing; Therefore get wisdom. And in all your getting, get understanding.

explanation.child: Look at the end of Proverbs 2:4.
explanation.teen: 4:7 is the setting; 2:4 has two lines, silver and then a second thing. Read the second.

teaching.extended_explanation: 2:4 first says to seek her as silver. 4:7 adds, “And in all your getting, get understanding.”
teaching.takeaway: Search for her “as for hidden treasures.”

prompt.adult: Agur says in 30:3 that he does not have knowledge of the Holy One. According to 25:2, what is the glory of kings?
prompt.child: One Proverb compares what brings glory to God with what brings glory to kings. What is the glory of kings?
prompt.teen: Proverbs 25:2: “But the glory of kings is” what?
prompt.older: Agur confesses in 30:3, “I neither learned wisdom.” What does 25:2 call the glory of kings?

choices.text: to judge the poor with justice

verses.text: It is the glory of God to conceal a matter, But the glory of kings is to search out a matter.
I neither learned wisdom Nor have knowledge of the Holy One.

explanation.child: Look at the end of verse 2.
explanation.teen: 30:3 is the setting; 25:2 sets God’s glory beside the glory of kings. Read the second line.

teaching.extended_explanation: 30:2 has Agur say he lacks the understanding of a man. 25:2 first names what is the glory of God.
teaching.takeaway: The glory of kings is “to search out a matter.”
